full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammed Habibur Rahman, J.:- This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to show cause why the proceedings in G.R. Case No. 529 of 1983 pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong arising out of Kotwali P.S. Case No. 67(4) 83 should not be quashed. 

 On the prayer of Mr. Nurul Islam Khan, Sub Inspector of Police, Kotwali P.S. Chittagong for extension of period of further investigation the learned Sessions Judge. Chittagong in exercise of his power under section 167(6) Cr.P.C. extended the period of further investigation upto 28-8-83 by passing an order on 26-7-83 in Criminal Misc. Case No. 619 of 1983 (permission). Thereafter on 25-8-83 the learned Sessions Judge on the prayer of Mr. Md. Hossain Ahmed Khan, Inspector, C.I.D. extended the period of investigation upto 27-9-83. Subsequently on the prayer of the said Inspector C.I.D. the learned Sessions Judge extended the period of further investigation upto 3-11-83 then upto 1-12-83 and then finally upto 26-12-83. The Police submitted charge sheet on 24-12-83 against accused Biswanath Basak (absconding) and accused petitioner Sabitri Rani Dey (on bail). Accused Tarun Kanti Chakrabarty and accused Ramani Mohan Basak were discharged. On 23-10-83 accused Sabitri Rani Dey had prayed before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for stopping the investigation under the provision of section 167(5) Cr.P.C. but the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate rejected the prayer by passing the following order on 23-10-83; 

 Thereafter on 2-11-83 accused Sabitri Rani Dey moved the Sessions Judge under section 438 Cr.P.C. for referring the matter to the High Court Division for setting aside the order dated 26-12-83 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate accepting the charge sheet and also quashing the proceedings in G.R. Case No. 529 of 1983. The learned Sessions Judge by his judgment dated 9-1-84 in Criminal Motion No. 715 of 1983 rejected the prayer for referring the matter to this Court. Thereafter the accused petitioner Sabitri Rani Dey obtained this Rule on 23-1-84. 

 The learned Advocate for the accused petitioner further argues that the learned Sessions Judge committed an illegality and acted without jurisdiction by passing a void order on 26-7-83 in Criminal Misc. Case No. 619 of 1983 erroneously exercising his power under section 167(6) Cr.P.C. extending the continuation of further investigation first upto 28-8-83 finally upto 26-12-83. The learned Advocate for the accused petitioner in short argues that unless the learned Magistrate in pursuance of the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. made an order stopping further investigation into the offence on the expiry of 29-7-83 and released the accused from custody if any under Sub-Section 7 of section 167 Cr.P.C. the learned Sessions Judge had no jurisdiction to exercise his power under Sub-section 6 of section 167 Cr.P.C. 

 From a plain reading of the entire provision of section 167 Cr.P.C. including its sub-section 6 it will appear that the Sessions Judge may not on an application made to him or otherwise, "where further investigation into an offence is stopped on the expiry either of the specified time or of the extended time under sub-section (5)." In the instant case the investigating police realised that it was not possible for them to complete the investigating on or before 29-7-83 and therefore made an irregular and premature petition under section 167(6) Cr.P.C. before the Sessions Judge who also irregularly by his order dated 26-7-83 extended the period of investigation in exercise of his power under section 167(6) Cr.P.C. The irregular order passing on 26-7-83 could have been set aside by this Court if the accused petitioner had come before us soon thereafter. But the right of the prosecution to move the Sessions Judge under sub-section 6 of section 167 Cr.P.C. accrued after the expiry of 29-7-83 for obtaining an order of further investigation and subsequently the learned Sessions Judge did pass various orders under section 167(6) Cr.P.C. extending the period of further investigation. It is to be deemed that on 29-7-83 the further proceedings were stopped in consequence of the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. Therefore although the order dated 26 7-83 of the learned Sessions Judge was irregular; but subsequent orders passed by him from 25-8-83 to 4-12-83 is quite in order and valid as he duly exercised his power under section 167(6) Cr.P.C. The charge sheet has been submitted by the police already on 24-12-83. At this stage the question of quashing the acceptance of the charge sheet dated 24-12-83 does not arise. The learned Advocate for the accused petitioner has not been able to make any ground for quashing the proceedings against the accused petitioner.
